status: preregistered before tests, systems measurement, or quality
scientific_question: Can sub-1%-state layer-private global frame motion align a broad shared nonlinear atom bank better than ten isolated private atoms?

causal_basis.deduction: isolated private atoms consumed too much state for too little width; spend private state on global transforms that move every shared detector and write direction

frozen_mechanism.paired_identity_initialization: reflectors 0/1 and 2/3 begin identical on each side, so both products begin at identity
frozen_mechanism.live_path: input and output Householder products are algebraically folded into the shared matrices; token activations use two dense GEMMs only
frozen_mechanism.initialization: input atoms use GPT c_fc std 0.02; output atoms are variance-corrected from width 3072 to width 312
frozen_mechanism.optimizer: Muon for the two shared matrices and AdamW for one-dimensional reflector/gain coordinates

gates.state_and_replay: exact and no dense MLP tensor, dense shadow, PCA basis, ambient code, persistent materialized transform, or duplicated shared state
gates.functional_equivalence: folded live function and all compact gradients equal explicit activation-space Householder products
gates.initialization: paired products and folded weights equal identity/original weights within numerical tolerance
gates.gradient: all live coordinates finite and nonzero; input/output reflector gradients are noncollapsed across layers

forbidden: width, reflector count, epsilon, initialization, seed, LR, optimizer, or gain sweeps
storing PCA basis vectors, dense shadow weights, materialized transforms, or ambient optimizer carry
